awd_titl_txt: Conference: VORTEX2025: Toward World Consensus on Vortex Definition and Prediction
awd_abstract_narration:
A vortex is a rotational or swirling motion in fluids. Vortices are ubiquitous in nature, and they are viewed as key components in fluid dynamics, especially turbulent flow. However, there is no precise mathematical definition of a vortex, which complicates research on vortical flows and turbulence.  This award will support a conference to be held December 11 – 13, 2025 at the University of Texas – Arlington.  The conference will promote exchanges among international scientists and engineers directed toward reaching a consensus on vortex definition and prediction. Vexing problems in a variety of fields such as oceanography, meteorology, astronomy and physiological fluid dynamics make achieving this goal especially urgent.  New ideas, methods, and applications related to vortex will be presented and discussed at this forum, and the results will be made widely available through publication of the conference proceedings.

The first definition of a vortex was given in 1858 by Helmholtz, who considered a vortex as a vorticity tube. Since then, a variety of vortex identification criteria have been used by fluid dynamics researchers.  This conference builds on a series of workshops and short courses aimed at vortex identification in engineering applications.  Topics addressed at the conference will include vortex definition and identification methods as well as applications in aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, biological flows, space science, and other disciplines.  The conference will be supplemented with a short course titled, “Liutex and Liutex-based subgrid models,” to be held immediately after the conference.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

Outcome Report to NSF for Conference Grant #2502481

Vortex2025 International Conference: Toward World Consensus on Vortex Definition and Prediction

Chaoqun Liu, Professor and Vortex 2025 Chair
University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, TX 76019

February 5, 2026

The International conference Vortex 2025, Toward World Consensus on Vortex Definition and Prediction, was successfully held in University of Texas at Arlington on December 13-17, 2025, under the support of the NSF and the University of Texas at Arlington.

As the conference announcement addressed, a vortex is intuitively recognized as the rotational/swirling motion of a fluid. Vortices are ubiquitous in nature and viewed as the building blocks, muscles, and sinews of turbulent flow. The mathematical definition of a vortex had been absent, and the lack of an accurate and quantifiable definition of a vortex is a hindrance to the study of fluid dynamics. This hybrid international conference aimed to facilitate academic exchanges among scientists and engineers worldwide toward a global consensus on the definition and prediction of vortices. Participants sought an accurate mathematical definition of a vortex in fluid dynamics through brainstorming among vortex researchers worldwide.

Ninety-eight people registered from 9 countries, including about 50 in-person and 48 online. There were 22 in-person and 22 online presentations, and 13 short-course students were supported by the National Science Foundation (NSF).  Among the 44 presentations, 28 reported their work on Liutex, including theory, methods, and applications to discover new physics. There were 12 invited speakers, including 6 international speakers. Among 11 invited speakers partially supported by the NSF, three of whom used Liutex methods. Participants came from different communities, including Mathematics, Mechanical Engineering, Geoscience, Space Science, Bioscience, and Chemical Engineering, and represent a wide range of fluid-related research areas including emerging fields such as deep machine learning and artificial intelligence.

Concluding Remarks

  1. Some consensus has been reached that Liutex is a rigorous mathematical definition for local fluid rotation or local vortex, which is endorsed almost unanimously by the scientific committee and vast majority of the participants with one exception who has different opinions.
  2. Vorticity decomposition to Liutex and shear by a rigorous mathematical formula, Vorticity = Liutex + Shear, is very important to quantify vortex and turbulence research.
  3. Liutex theory and methods have been widely applied by researchers in different research areas including aerodynamics, hydrodynamics, thermal dynamics, hemodynamics, atmosphere science, etc. to do the vortex identification and discover new physics in their own areas.
  4. There are many scientific research activities ongoing in the vortex dynamics around the world.
  5. The definition for global fluid rotation or natural vortex is complicated, and a world consensus is hard to reach during a single conference. More time and effort are needed to find a definition for a natural vortex/global fluid rotation.
